## TL;DR

A phone now has one task detail: the shared `TaskDrawer`, mounted once by `App.vue` for every entry point. The read-only `MobileTaskDetail` stub is gone. Below 720px the drawer becomes a full-screen phone page with labelled 44×44 Back and close controls, a scrollable seven-tab strip, 44px controls, 16px inputs and a Paused state with **Resume work**. Queue cards, Search, notices, `?task=<id>&tab=…` deep links and post-create converge on it. Review round 1 found a route/queue desync while a deep link loaded or failed; one surface computed plus restored shells fixed it.

## Work and rationale

The bug was structural. `App.vue` hid `TaskDrawer` whenever a narrow `/work?task=` route was active and `WorkView` rendered `MobileTaskDetail` instead. That stub had no review report, PM chat, Changes/Dev/Debug tabs, edit fields or most actions, so a task told different stories depending on where it was opened. Patching it to parity would have preserved two state machines and guaranteed drift, so the drawer's phone mode became the single detail.

`WorkView`'s narrow branch now owns the queue and the phone loading/not-found state; the queue stays mounted with `v-show` so Back is instant and filter/sort state survives. `App.vue` always mounts `TaskDrawer` and hides `MobileTabs` only while a task is open.

Route ownership needed care. On desktop the drawer opens and immediately clears `?task=`; on a phone that param is the detail-page address and must stay so browser Back works. Because the drawer is global, every close path (X, Escape, overlay, an action calling `ui.close()`) drops `task` and `tab` through a watcher on open state. The phone Back control replaces `/work` when the drawer was opened there and pushes `/work` from another page.

Pause was the one state the drawer did not model. `repo.pauseWork` records the task in `pausedIds` immediately, but `runningIds` may still contain it until the process exits, and the status card ignored `isPaused`. I added a `workPaused` key to the drawer status priority above `workRunning` (excluding PM activity). The status line reads “Paused”, the Pause button disappears as soon as the POST returns, and the primary action becomes **Resume work**, disabled only while the old process is still stopping. `pausedIds` is seeded from `/api/agents/running` on load, so it survives a reload. I also surfaced Acknowledge in the drawer quickbar for fresh-done and AI-created tasks; with the queue card covered they otherwise had no phone path.

The phone chrome is CSS-only below 720px. The drawer fills `100vw`; the header title column shrinks (`min-width: 0`) so long chips cannot push the close off-screen; Back and close are 44×44 with accessible names; tabs, quickbar, agent picker, canned prompts and inputs meet the 44px/16px floors. It clips with `overflow-x: clip` rather than `hidden`, which would create a scroll container that a programmatic focus can shift, taking the close with it.

## Review round 1 fix

The review found that the queue was hidden on the `?task=` string alone while `ui.active` did not exist yet. A slow deep-link fetch left a blank page, and a failed fetch hid the queue with no surface at all.

`WorkView` now derives the phone surface from one state. `phoneTaskParam` is the normalised, non-`new` id; `phoneTaskPending` means that id is present but no drawer task is open; `mobileDetailVisible` covers the open drawer, the new-task panel and the pending state. The queue shows only when it is false, so it is never hidden without a real surface above it. Pending renders a full-page loading shell while `ui.activeDetailLoading` is true and a “Task unavailable” shell with a 44px **Return to Work** action when loading finishes without a task.

A per-route `taskOpenRequest` token closes the related race: a late fetch cannot open an old task or clear a newer request's loading flag. Tests cover pending, not-found/return, and a stale fetch resolving after the user left.

## Approaches tried

Growing `MobileTaskDetail` to parity was rejected: it would duplicate the drawer's status priority, review rendering, PM/Dev sessions, diff viewer and edit flow. Replacing the stub inside `WorkView` was also rejected because Search, notices and new-task open `ui.active` without a Work route; only a single mount above the router makes every entry point identical.

For the tab strip I used the existing `drawer-tabs-scroll` opt-in class rather than making `.drawer-tabs` scroll globally; the story panel already uses it and applying it only when narrow keeps desktop unchanged. For paused state I considered deriving it from “not running”; that is wrong while an agent is still exiting and cannot distinguish a pause from a crash.

For verification I extended the existing WebKit smoke. It opens `/work?task=9001&tab=changes` at 360px and checks body overflow, 44×44 labelled Back/close, the selected Changes tab, last-tab reachability after scrolling, a 16px composer and 44px canned prompts/agent picker. Component tests cover entry-point parity, deep-link tab selection, close-clears-route, Paused/Resume, pending/not-found shells, stale fetches, and a failed reviewer keeping **Review again** reachable.

## Challenges and blockers

The main subtlety was the two route models. A `?task=` URL is transient control state on desktop but a page address on a phone. Clearing it in the wrong place either re-opens the drawer after a dismiss or leaves a stale refreshable task URL. The solution keeps desktop's clear-on-open behaviour and clears on every phone close route while preserving Back.

I have no physical phone. Verification is headless WebKit at 360/390px (geometry, overflow, tab reachability, composer font size) plus jsdom component tests at 360/390/412. The 16px rule prevents the reported iOS zoom, but the physical-device pass belongs to sibling #1139.

## Key learnings

One detail component is the only durable fix for entry-point parity; a second mobile stub guarantees future disagreement.

A route param can be transient UI state or a page address depending on layout. The detail owner must clear it on every close path and must not treat the param as proof that a surface exists. Async loads tied to that route need a request token so a late result cannot re-open an old task or clear a newer loading state.

An explicit `pausedIds` signal beats inferring a pause from a stopped process; keep its action disabled until the old process exits.
